theme: General order quality issues / no resolution offered
observed: 157 reviews describe negative order experiences with no consistent single root cause — spanning delayed orders, unfulfilled promises, and unresolved complaints, unified mainly by extremely low ratings (97% at 1-2★) and a shared sense that Swiggy did not resolve the issue.
inferred: This is likely several distinct, smaller problems that clustering couldn't separate cleanly — not one single root cause. The one common thread is a resolution gap: customers consistently report that nothing was done after the initial problem occurred.
unknown: What the actual root causes are within this cluster (needs finer-grained analysis), and whether 'no resolution' reflects a policy gap or an execution gap.
next_step: This cluster is too broad to act on directly. Before treating it as one opportunity, re-cluster just these 157 reviews at a higher cluster count, or manually sample 30-40 to identify the real sub-themes hiding inside it.

theme: Wrong or incomplete item delivered
observed: 58 reviews specifically describe receiving the wrong item, a missing item, or an incomplete order — a distinct, specific failure mode separate from delivery timing.
inferred: This points to an order-fulfillment accuracy problem, likely on the restaurant/dark-store packing side rather than the delivery/logistics side, given the specificity of 'wrong item' vs. 'late item' language.
unknown: Whether this concentrates in specific restaurant partners, specific cities, or specific order types (Instamart vs. food delivery) — no restaurant- or city-level data is available to check this.
next_step: Cross-reference this signal against internal order-accuracy or restaurant-partner-quality data — 58 independent, specific complaints is strong enough evidence to justify checking against data Swiggy already has internally.

theme: Delivery delays attributed to slow/unavailable delivery partners
observed: 51 reviews specifically attribute delays to a lack of available delivery partners, not to restaurant prep time or app issues.
inferred: May indicate a supply-side (delivery partner capacity) problem concentrated at certain times or locations, rather than a demand-forecasting or app-UX problem.
unknown: Whether this clusters by time of day (several quotes suggest late night) or by geography — no timestamp-pattern analysis or location data available to confirm.
next_step: Cross-reference against internal delivery-partner-supply data by hour and region — if this is a real, time-concentrated supply gap, that's directly actionable operationally.

theme: Restaurant/delivery network unable to fulfill orders on time
observed: 23 reviews describe orders that could not be fulfilled or delivered as promised by the restaurant/delivery network, distinct from generic lateness.
inferred: May reflect restaurant-side capacity or coordination issues rather than a Swiggy-app-side problem.
unknown: Whether specific restaurants or categories are overrepresented in this pattern.
next_step: Cross-reference against restaurant-level fulfillment-rate data if available internally.

theme: Cancellation fee charged unfairly or disproportionately
observed: 23 reviews describe being charged a cancellation fee in situations they perceive as unfair — either Swiggy itself cancelled the order, or the customer cancelled within a very short window.
inferred: The cancellation fee policy, or its application, may not be clearly communicated or may not account for near-immediate cancellations and Swiggy-initiated cancellations.
unknown: What the actual policy is, whether these are policy violations or the policy working as designed but perceived as unfair, and whether this is a small vocal minority or a broader pattern.
next_step: This is a policy-clarity question, not a product-bug question — recommend a policy review informed by these specific complaint patterns.

theme: No response from chat support / follow-ups ignored
observed: 23 reviews specifically describe the support channel itself failing — bot-only responses, no path to a human agent, or messages going unanswered — as the central complaint.
inferred: The AI/bot-first support flow may lack an adequate escalation path to human agents for cases where the bot can't resolve the issue.
unknown: What percentage of support interactions this affects, and whether an escalation path exists but isn't surfaced to users, vs. not existing at all.
next_step: Interview a small sample of affected users to understand exactly where they got stuck in the support flow.

theme: Delivery partner unresponsive, rude, or fails to deliver as described
observed: 16 reviews describe specific behavioral complaints about individual delivery partners — refusing instructions, rudeness, or unresponsiveness — distinct from generic delay complaints.
inferred: May reflect a training or accountability gap for delivery partner conduct, though 16 signals is a small sample.
unknown: Whether these are isolated individual incidents or a systemic pattern.
next_step: Given low volume but high severity (100% at ≤2★), interview 5-8 affected users directly before deciding this warrants operational action.

theme: Refund denied or money not returned for valid claims
observed: 28 reviews describe a refund being explicitly requested and denied, as the central complaint.
inferred: There may be a gap between what customers consider a 'genuine' refund case and Swiggy's actual refund-eligibility criteria — or a gap in how that criteria is communicated.
unknown: What Swiggy's actual refund policy says in these specific scenarios, and whether these are policy-consistent denials or genuine policy misapplications.
next_step: Cross-reference a sample against internal refund-decision logs, if available, to determine whether the fix is a policy change or a communication change.
